title: SYSK's 2025 Holiday Extravaganza Christmas Special
summary: Holiday special of Stuff You Should Know with no ads. The hosts open with a Christmas drink segment (Chuck's pumpkin spice Old Fashioned and homemade syrup), then cover Moravian putz/Christmas villages and the origin of trains around the tree, the Frost Fairs held on the frozen Thames in London, Vince Guaraldi and the Charlie Brown Christmas music, the Welsh Mari Lwyd tradition, and tips for storing Christmas tree lights.
topics: Cast Your Fate to the Wind

entities.name: Cast Your Fate to the Wind

segments.title: Opening banter and no-ads holiday special
segments.summary: Hosts welcome listeners to the annual holiday special, note there are no ads this episode, and tease Chuck's holiday drink.

segments.title: Moravian putz and Christmas villages
segments.summary: The hosts describe how Moravian settlers in the Lehigh Valley of Pennsylvania expanded Nativity scenes into elaborate putz displays, the family putz room tradition, mid-20th-century artist Jenny Train, and how the Christmas village evolved into the origin of trains around the tree with Lionel electric trains.

segments.title: Chuck's pumpkin spice Old Fashioned
segments.summary: Chuck walks through his homemade pumpkin spice syrup recipe (sugar-water ratios, spice blend, boiling and cooling), the Old Fashioned build with bourbon and bitters, and the orange peel and cinnamon garnish techniques.

segments.title: Frost Fairs on the frozen Thames
segments.summary: The hosts explain London's Frost Fairs, held when the Thames froze during the Little Ice Age, enabled by narrow arches of the old London Bridge and a wider, shallower river. They cover the 1564 and 1607-08 freezes, the 1683-84 fair with John Evelyn's description, food and drink such as roast ox and wormwood wine, the 1814 final fair, and a 1962 freeze.

segments.title: Vince Guaraldi and the Charlie Brown Christmas music
segments.summary: Biography of jazz pianist Vince Guaraldi, born Vincent Dalaglio in San Francisco, his early jazz career and Art Tatum connection, the song Cast Your Fate to the Wind, and how Lee Mendelssohn commissioned music for A Boy Named Charlie Brown that led to the Charlie Brown Christmas special, plus its later honors.
topics: Cast Your Fate to the Wind

segments.title: Mari Lwyd, the Welsh horse tradition
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Mari Lwyd, a Welsh Christmas tradition in which a hobby horse with a skull-like head goes house to house for a sung verse battle, the luck it brings, the Christian and pagan origins of its name, and its 19th-century revival.

segments.title: Storing Christmas tree lights
segments.summary: The hosts share internet tips for storing Christmas lights on cardboard tubes, rectangular cardboard, coffee caddies, and Chuck's method of bagging each strand separately, along with Josh's extension-cord-style wrapping.

segments.title: Holiday sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wish listeners happy holidays, mention loneliness during the season, and sign off.
